# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).
data.title: Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Problem

Duplicate work items are created by e2e tests running against the real worklog DB:
- `tests/e2e/headless-tui.test.ts`: 'Test item for show' (265) + 'Test item for show JSON' (266) — 531 items created 08-01..08-07, no cleanup teardown. Still present in 3 stale worktrees.
- `tests/e2e/agent-flow.test.ts`: 'Test E2E item from agent pipeline' (43) — created 05-21, all deleted.

Sync-clobber bug reverts soft-deletes (known in WL-0MSPZP7FE009YXPG), and `wl doctor prune` has never been run (778 soft-deleted items accumulate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1**: `tests/e2e/headless-tui.test.ts` has teardown that deletes created items (or the test is removed if no longer needed)
- [ ] **AC2**: `tests/e2e/agent-flow.test.ts` has teardown that deletes created items
- [ ] **AC3**: Stale worktrees (align-icons, grid-rebalance, wire-read-commands) are pruned or their copies of these tests are deleted
- [ ] **AC4**: All 284 open 'Test item for show'/'…JSON' items are deleted and verified gone after sync
- [ ] **AC5**: `wl doctor prune --days 0` removes all remaining soft-deleted items (778 total)
- [ ] **AC6**: Post-fix `wl sync` shows no sync conflicts for these items (remote state matches)

## Implementation Notes

1. Add teardown to headless-tui test: capture created item IDs, call `wl delete <id>` in `afterEach`/`afterAll`
2. Same for agent-flow test
3. Check if stale worktrees are needed; if not, `wl doctor prune-worktree <dir>` or manual cleanup
4. Re-delete open items, sync, verify remote
5. Run `wl doctor prune --days 0` on both local and remote branches
data.title: Fix: add test-teardown guard, clean up stale worktrees, and run prune

data.description:
## Problem

`wl doctor prune --days N` hard-deletes items locally, but the next `wl sync` re-adds them all from the remote ref, because `mergeWorkItems` (src/sync.ts) re-imports every remote item missing locally (`if (!localItem) { mergedMap.set(remoteItem.id, remoteItem); }`). There is no `--no-pull` and prune has no push/rewrite path.

## Observed (2026-08-13)

- Ran `wl doctor prune --days 0` → 1,034 items hard-deleted locally (2941 → 1907 items)
- Ran `wl sync` → 'Work items added: 1034' — all resurrected from `refs/worklog/data` (back to 2941)
- Net result: prune is a no-op in a synced setup; items remain soft-deleted forever (the 'deleted but not pruned' backlog)

## Proposed fix

Add `--push` (or auto-push) to `wl doctor prune` that, after hard-deleting locally, rewrites the remote worklog ref with the pruned local state — mirroring `doctor foreign-items --apply --push` which already uses `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile` (src/sync.ts:1130).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl doctor prune --days N --push` leaves the remote ref without the pruned items
- [ ] A subsequent `wl sync` does NOT resurrect the pruned items
- [ ] `--dry-run` unchanged; default remains no-push (safe)
- [ ] Unit/integration test covers prune+push against a temp git repo
data.title: wl doctor prune cannot persist: sync re-adds pruned items from remote ref

# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`
- Non-terminal transitions (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must NOT change priority

### Key Files
- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — helper function location
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — priority constants
data.title: Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal

Wire the hydrator into the worklist plugin (packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts) as a TaskScheduler task, visibility-gated, with an immediate run when the tab regains focus (reusing the existing resume-poll machinery). No second interval loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A scheduler task id 'hydrate' is registered on the existing TaskScheduler with intervalMs 30_000, singleFlight: true, and runTimeoutMs set; a rejecting task never takes down the scheduler loop.
2. The hydrate task is visibility-gated: while the worklist pane is hidden it does not run and spawns zero wl processes (paneGate pattern).
3. On a hidden→visible transition, hydration runs immediately (in addition to the existing refresh) without waiting for the next 30s tick.
4. Hydrator deps are injected into worklist.ts (e.g. via opts) so tests can substitute fakes.
5. Full project suite passes; no regressions in existing worklist tests.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts — register hydrate task + resume hook
- packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts — reused as-is
- packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts — reuse PollGate/paneGate
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — visibility-gated scheduler precedent

## Minimal Implementation

1. Register hydrate task alongside refresh/sync/resume-poll/downtime with the same interval/visibility wiring used by the downtime worker.
2. In the resume-poll hidden→visible transition branch, invoke the hydrate task immediately (parallel to the existing immediate refresh).

## Dependencies

- Requires F2 (hydrator module — runHydrationOnce to invoke)
data.title: Worklist: hydrate task + focus-resume

## Goal

Implement the herdr hydrator module (packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts): every 30s (and on worklist focus-resume) it fetches all in_progress work items, matches each against work-item IDs in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace, and demotes any item with no matching pane per the signal-based rule (AC3 of parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI). Pure decision functions + orchestration with injectable deps; fail-open at every boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes) returns WL-[0-9A-Z]+ IDs found in pane labels.
2. isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes) returns true iff the ID appears in a running pane's label in any tab of the current workspace; workspace filtering via herdr pane list --workspace <id> / HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID env var.
3. decideDemotion(workItem, blockers): stage in_review → {status: completed, stage: in_review}; active outbound blocker (target not completed/deleted, stage not in_review/done, per isDependencyActive in packages/shared/src/database.ts) → {status: blocked, stage: plan_complete (or best compatible)}; else → {status: open, stage: intake_complete}; stage always chosen per src/config.ts compatibility.
4. runHydrationOnce(deps): fetches wl list --status in_progress, fetches panes, computes demotions, applies each via wl update (status+stage); an item with a matching pane is never touched.
5. Fail-open: wl/pane CLI missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output → skip the entire cycle with a log; the function never throws; no demotion happens on untrustworthy evidence.
6. All hydrator.test.ts tests pass; full project suite passes.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts — new module
- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts — reuse runWl/extractJson/extractItems
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — orchestration precedent
- src/commands/dep.ts + packages/shared/src/database.ts — dependency semantics (reference only)
- src/config.ts — status/stage compatibility (reference only)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Pure helpers: extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles, isActivePaneMatch, decideDemotion (status, stage) pair.
2. runHydrationOnce(deps) with injectable {runWl, runPaneList, now, log}; fetch in_progress; fetch panes filtered to workspace; outbound-edge stage fetch per blocker candidate (wl dep list carries status only — fetch stage via wl show for each edge not completed/deleted).
3. Apply demotions; wrap whole cycle in try/catch that logs and returns without demoting.

## Dependencies

- Requires F1 (hydrator.test.ts — written first; suite must pass to close)
- Requires F0 (pane-title format amendment — ID must survive truncation)
data.title: Hydrator: demote stale in_progress items

# Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`) and the Herdr extension selection list (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` → `worklist.ts`) disagree on "most important item" because the dispatcher maintains its own tier ordering (`wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` audit query) instead of reusing the Herdr list. The project needs the dispatcher to consume the Herdr list head so the two selectors agree by construction. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`" scope per producer determination WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 (2026-09-02).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy queue; the item dispatched during downtime was visible at the top of `prefix+l` and reflects declared prioritization intent.
- **Herdr user browsing `prefix+l`** — expects downtime work to track exactly what the visible list shows, so automated work does not appear arbitrary.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl next** — needs a single ranking contract; ranking logic lives only in the fetcher/smart-selection/grouping/database pipeline.

Example user stories:
- As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher to pick the first item shown in the Herdr list, so automated work follows the priority I already see.
- As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been at the head of the Herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen.
- As a maintainer, I want the ranking contract documented as "dispatcher == Herdr list head" so future safety gates are evaluated as filters, not a competing ranking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head** — `dispatchDowntimeWork` (and any coordination-leader path) derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head rather than a separate tier ordering / stage-scoped `wl next` / `wl list` audit query. No second ranking implementation remains on the dispatch path.
2. **No duplicate ranking; gates are filters** — tier ordering / `wl next --stage` per-tier calls / audit `wl list` ranking are no longer used to pick "most important". Any safety gates that must remain (code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight / CAS claim) act as sequential filters on the Herdr-ordered candidates. If no Herdr-ordered candidate passes the filters, the dispatcher reports "no candidate" rather than falling back to a separate ranking.
3. **Herdr list remains sole ranking path** — `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` stay the sole ranking path (mandatory-always for critical + `completed`/`in_review`, `browseItemCount` windowing of "other" items, grouping logic, `reSort`/`computeScore` as used by the fetcher). No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change is required to fix the divergence; if `fetchNextItems` delegates to `wl next` internally that internal detail is acceptable — the observable contract is "dispatcher == Herdr list head".
4. **Contract documented** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` (and `src/commands/next.ts` help if it references dispatcher selection) state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list; any remaining safety override (e.g. code-freeze) is documented as a skip/filter on that sequence, not a ranking.
5. **No regression; observable agreement proven** — existing `wl next` / herdr fetcher/grouping / downtime-worker fixtures pass; a reproducible sampling script shows `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree (downtime picks the list head after filtering) on a fixture. Dispatched-marker / code-freeze / single-flight gating still respected as filters on the Herdr sequence.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr; `smart-selection.ts`/`grouping.ts` duplicated per TUI stays in sync with `src/commands/*` if touched.
- `browseItemCount` clamping (1–50) and root-only / `done`-exclusion rules respected.
- Do not fork a second ranking; reuse the Herdr list pipeline.
- Investigation only touched the prior item (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q); this item carries the implementation.
- Backwards compat: existing dispatched-marker / code-freeze gating semantics preserved as filters.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets via `fetchMandatorySubsets` (`wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`), applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review). Rendered via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order audit → implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete` with risk/effort caps) → plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`) → fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` with 7-day recency / dispatched-marker / active-audit / code-freeze gates; pre-dispatch CAS claim, per-process single-flight, scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin cursor, cooldowns.
- **Shared scoring:** `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (`computeScore`/`reSort`/`filterCandidates`/`findNextWorkItemFromItems`) and `src/commands/next.ts` auto `reSort` — shared by `wl next` but not required to change for this contract; the observable contract is Herdr list head.
- All divergence gaps mapped in WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q (cap 32 / mandatory merge / stage-scoped calls / audit `wl list` source / tier order / risk-effort gates / code-freeze tri-state, etc.) — eliminated by consuming the Herdr order directly.

## Desired change

Replace the dispatcher's independent tier ordering with consumption of the Herdr selection list head:

- Refactor `downtime-worker.ts` to invoke (or share code with) the Herdr fetcher/selection pipeline to obtain the ordered candidate sequence, then apply only the necessary safety filters (code-freeze, dispatched-marker, single-flight/active-audit) sequentially on that sequence.
- Remove or dead-code the tier-ordering / per-stage `wl next` / audit `wl list` ranking path from the dispatch decision (or leave only as unused fallback behind a feature flag with a clear deprecation note).
- Document the contract ("dispatcher == Herdr list head; filters, not ranking") in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Herdr selection pipeline reused by dispatcher
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — mandatory-always + browseItemCount logic
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — regroupWorkItems / assignItemGroups ordering
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — rendering consuming grouped selection
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatchDowntimeWork to be refactored to consume list head (+ fixtures)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — computeScore/reSort/filterCandidates as used by fetcher (not dispatcher ranking)
- `src/commands/next.ts` / `src/commands/grouping.ts` — wl next entry point as used by fetcher
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher contract doc
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr list contract doc

## Related work

- Investigation: WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q — downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list divergence (producer determination revised 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, superseding WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS) → follow-up direction is this item.
- WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX — counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect (symptom of cap/mandatory interaction; not blocking but shares fetcher context)
- WL-0MS8XL3EW006Y04G / WL-0MSKCRX730052iiw / WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G / WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR — Herdr smart selection / in_review / root-only rules shaping mandatory set
- WL-0MSMAYPQP001FLR6 / WL-0MSMAIP5F003WAGG — implement tier + risk/effort filters wired into wl next / dispatcher (removed or converted to filters in this work)
- WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY / WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN / WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 — dispatched-marker exclusion, conditional claim, dispatch logging (preserved as filters)
- WL-0MSSRED76008LGB6 — priority-first with round-robin tie-break (cursor handling to reconcile with Herdr order)
- RCA docs: `downtime-redispatch-rca-2026-08-13.md`, `downtime-disable-incident-rca-2026-08-22.md` — prior tier/re-dispatch incidents

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "selection list" means herdr `prefix+l` Work Items list (`fetchNextItems` path); "downtime dispatcher" means `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier loop in `downtime-worker.ts` (including coordination leader path if any).
- Assumption: producer wants a single notion of "most important" — confirmed 2026-09-02 (Herdr list canonical; dispatcher consumes head).
- Risk: code-freeze / audit safety behavior at head — if the list head must be skipped, the skip order must be explicit and remain a filter on the Herdr sequence; document clearly.
- Risk: `in_review` mandatory-always items in the list — dispatcher taking the head must still respect `completed`/`in_review` dispatchability; filter vs ranking distinction must be explicit to avoid re-dispatching audits.
- Risk: spare-capacity / idle-budget / round-robin cursor logic must be reconciled as filters or removed; otherwise a second ordering re-emerges.
- Scope-creep risk: unifying ranking touches herdr selection and downtime-worker — keep scope to dispatcher-consumes-head; do not rework scoring or grouping unless required for the contract. Extra opportunities → new work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When you say 'most important,' do you mean the Herdr list order or the dispatcher tier order?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1, rescoping WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2; supersedes WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS): **Herdr extension selection list order is authoritative** (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). Dispatcher selects the first item in that list — no second ranking. Source: producer comment WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.
- Q2: "Should the two selectors be unified to one shared ranking, or should the dispatcher intentionally differ (e.g. audit-first)?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **Unified on the Herdr list** — single source of truth; dispatcher consumes the list head. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`". Source: same producer determination.
- Q3: "For sampling, which `browseItemCount` / `wl next -n` window and which worklog root should be the reference?" — Answer (Producer, 2026-09-02, WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS as affirmed by WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1): **LGTM** — default `browseItemCount` / ContextHub root / `wl next -n 20` accepted as sampling reference. Source: producer comment on WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q.

No open questions. Interview skipped — seed context and revised producer determination (WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1) already provide a clear, testable brief.
data.title: Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (supersedes wl next unification)

Discovered while finishing WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6 (docs-only) — discovered-from: WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6.

The pane-run log line produced by send-to-pi.sh embeds the realpath of run-pi-agent.sh (resolved from the script's own location). tests/herdr/send-to-pi.test.ts 'omits --model from the pi invocation when not provided' asserts:

  expect(run).not.toContain('code');

When the checkout/worktree path contains the substring 'code' (e.g. the worktree slug ...colour-code-work-items-by-priority-in-se), the embedded script path trips this assertion even though --model is correctly omitted. On the main checkout (/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub, no 'code' in path) the test passes 10/10 and the full suite is green.

Fix options: assert on the forwarded pi args (portion after the exec bash <script> path) rather than the raw log line, or assert no standalone 'code' token after --model handling.

# Child 1: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) runs `UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` (unless `--no-re-sort`), on create/update, so routine queue reads rewrite `updatedAt` on dozens of items at once (observed: 13 items at `2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z`, 88 items at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`).

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit. Concrete victim: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V audited "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03 now carries `updatedAt` 2026-09-11, so its passing audit reads stale and the item lingers in the open queue. Recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`) is also polluted.

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** a "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical re-sorts.
- **Heartbeat/audit pipeline:** must not re-audit items whose only change is sortIndex.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` (and the `database.ts:755-767` single-item re-sort path) no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- [ ] Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run `reSort`, assert the audit is still fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt` holds / freshness check passes) and `updatedAt` is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 behavior preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Check sibling: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` — `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:755-793` — re-sort paths; `:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`; `:2215` — recency scoring
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts`

## Related work

Discovered-from: WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH.

When the audit runner runs child audits in separate-process mode (`--no-child-in-main-slot`), each child Phase-1 AC screen spawned a pi subprocess whose output could not be parsed: 'Warning: Unparseable Pi output for AC evaluation — falling back to partial verdict'. All child ACs were persisted as partial ('Ready to close: No'), which then reverted the in_review children to open/plan_complete and (via dependency reconciliation) to blocked — cascading a parent audit to 'Ready to close: No' even though the parent's own ACs were all met.

The default in-main-slot mode avoids this (child screens are performed by the invoking session), which is how the parent was ultimately verified green. Suggest: make separate-process child screening resilient to the local-proxy output format (or detect the unparseable case and retry/escalate instead of persisting partial), so the mode is usable in this environment.

# Intake Brief — Smart Audit Re-instatement

**Headline:** When the audit freshness check (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`) flags an audit as stale, the system should automatically review the changes made since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or flag the item for re-audit — rather than treating all post-audit changes as requiring a full re-run.

## Problem statement

Audits are invalidated whenever a work item's `updatedAt` changes after the audit time (`isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`). However, many changes do not affect the code or implementation that was audited (e.g., changing a comment, updating assignee). The audit skill should automatically inspect the changes since the audit and decide whether to re-instate the original audit or require a new one.

**Producer clarification:** The system should inspect anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it — description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl next` / Pi TUI:** Audited items should not be unnecessarily re-audited when changes are irrelevant to the implementation.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited and whose changes are non-semantic.
- **Producers:** A "Ready to close: Yes" item should stay ready unless changes actually affect the audit outcome.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Automatic re-instatement detection:** When `isAuditNotReadyFresh` returns `false` (audit flagged as stale), the system automatically inspects the changes made since `auditedAt` and decides whether to re-instate the audit or flag for re-audit.
2. **Change inspection covers key fields:** The inspection examines description, comments, audit text, dependencies, and commit messages for changes that could affect the audit outcome. Non-semantic changes (e.g., metadata-only updates) do not trigger re-audit.
3. **Re-instatement logic:** If changes are deemed non-semantic (no impact on audit outcome), the original audit is re-instated by resetting `updatedAt` to `auditedAt` (same pattern as `saveAuditResult`). If changes are semantic, the audit is flagged as needing re-run.
4. **Full project test suite passes** with new regression tests covering re-instatement of non-semantic changes and re-audit flag for semantic changes.

## Constraints

- Change confined to audit freshness logic in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` and the audit result management in the persistent store.
- No schema changes required.
- Must preserve existing audit behavior for items with no previous audit.
- Must be fully automatic — no operator intervention required.

## Existing state

- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:644`** — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt`. If false, the audit is treated as stale.
- **`packages/shared/src/database.ts:1038`** — `saveAuditResult` resets `updatedAt = auditedAt` to keep audits fresh after audit writes.
- **`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`** — Audit results stored in SQLite; `getAllAuditResults` / `saveAuditResult` methods.

## Desired change

1. Create a new function `assessAuditInvalidate(changesSinceAudited, auditResult)` that inspects the delta between the audit time and current state.
2. The function should classify changes as semantic (affect audit outcome) or non-semantic (no impact).
3. For non-semantic changes, re-instate the audit (reset `updatedAt = auditedAt`).
4. For semantic changes, mark the audit as needing re-run.
5. Integrate into the `wl next` / TUI flow where audit freshness is checked.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh` (line 644), audit map builder, sorting logic
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — Audit storage methods, `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line 747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` — Sync merge logic
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — Audit command integration point
- `src/pi-audit.ts` — Pi audit module

## Related work

- **WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO** — Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations (complementary; prevents timestamp churn, this handles post-invalidation review)
- **WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA** — Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn (child of WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO)
- **WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5** — Established the audit freshness rule (`auditedAt >= updatedAt`)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Semantic boundary ambiguity:** What counts as a semantic change is subjective. **Assumption:** Changes to description, comments, dependencies, and commit messages are semantic; changes to assignee, tags, priority, and sortIndex are non-semantic. Document the rule in code comments.
- **Scope creep:** Requests for configurable invalidation policies. **Mitigation:** Keep this to the concrete scenarios identified; file separate items for broader policy changes.
- **Performance risk:** Inspecting changes since audit could add overhead. **Mitigation:** Only run when freshness check fails; use efficient diff comparison.
- **Backward compatibility:** Existing audit behavior must be preserved for items with no previous audit result.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What specific change types should the audit skill inspect when deciding whether to re-instate an audit? — A: Anything that changes the intent of the work item or actions taken against it. So description, comments, audit text, dependencies, commit messages etc. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: Should this be automatic (triggered when an invalidated audit is discovered) or manual (operator/producer-initiated)? — A: Automatic. Source: interactive reply (producer).
- Q: How does this relate to WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO (Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations)? — A: Complementary — WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO prevents timestamp churn from invalidating audits, this item handles post-invalidation review to determine whether to re-instate or re-run. Source: interactive reply (producer).

Same latent hermeticity defect as WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI, found while fixing it: several worklist test files match herdr CLI calls with `bin === 'herdr'`. Because `isPaneVisible()` / pane helpers resolve the CLI as `process.env.HERDR_BIN_PATH ?? 'herdr'`, those mocks silently miss whenever the suite runs inside a herdr pane (which sets HERDR_BIN_PATH to an absolute path), and the call falls through to the mock's generic branch — which can flip a visibility probe to fail-open 'visible'.

Verified call sites (argument-based matching is the fix): packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts:114, worklist-agent-state.test.ts:78, worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts:121,200, worklist-icons.test.ts:89, worklist-inflight.test.ts:102, worklist-nested-expand.test.ts:128, fetcher-timeout.test.ts:113,374.

Currently non-blocking: the full suite is green (the affected assertions do not depend on the missed branch), so this is hardening, not a live failure. Discovered from: WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI.

# Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher creates panes for each work item it dispatches (intake, plan, audit, risk-effort), but panes stay open indefinitely until an operator closes them manually. There is no automatic pane lifecycle management — completed panes clutter the Dispatcher workspace and the dispatch log lacks pane-close status updates (intake complete, plan complete, audit passed/failed, or stuck). This work item adds automatic pane closing and enhanced logging for pane lifecycle events.

## Users

- **Operator** — wants the Dispatcher workspace to stay tidy; auto-closed panes reduce manual cleanup.
- **Producer** — wants a clear audit trail of pane outcomes in the dispatch log: which panes completed successfully, which are stuck, and which failed their audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The downtime worker logs every pane-close event to `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` with: ISO timestamp, work item ID, work item title, pane ID, dispatch kind (`plan`/`intake`/`audit`/`risk-effort`), and outcome (`closed-as-intake-complete`, `closed-as-plan-complete`, `audit-passed`, `audit-failed`, `requires-attention`).
- **AC2:** When a dispatched item's stage advances to `intake_complete` or `plan_complete`, the worker records the appropriate log entry and closes the associated pane (except for `kind === 'implement'` items).
- **AC3:** When a dispatched item is left in any other state (e.g. `in_review` without reaching a terminal state, or blocked by producer questions where `needsProducerReview === true`), the worker records a `requires-attention` log entry with a summary reason.
- **AC4:** When a dispatched item reaches `in_review` status (implementation completed), the worker records the event in the log.
- **AC5:** When an audit pane completes and the item's audit status is recorded (`auditedAt` set, audit passed or failed), the worker records the audit outcome in the log and closes the pane (audit panes are always auto-closed regardless of the `implement` exception).
- **AC6:** The `implement` kind is EXCLUDED from all auto-close logic — implement panes remain open until manually closed by the operator.
- **AC7:** All logging and pane-closing operations are fail-closed: a failed log write or pane-close attempt must never crash the worker or block subsequent dispatches.
- **AC8:** Full herdr + repo test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The existing `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` rolling JSONL format must be extended (not replaced); legacy entries remain valid.
- Pane closing must be safe — only panes that were spawned by the downtime worker for this specific work item should be closed.
- The worker must detect state changes without polling the worklog excessively; consider event-driven or reasonable polling cadence.
- The `implements` exception (AC6) is mandatory — no implement pane is ever auto-closed.

## Existing state

- Dispatch logging already exists via `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8): a bounded JSONL log recording dispatched items.
- The `AgentTracker` (`agent-tracker.ts`) already records work-item → pane-ID associations in `.worklog/agent-panes.json`.
- Panes are spawned via `send-to-pi.sh` with pane IDs that are captured and tracked.
- Panes currently stay open indefinitely — no auto-close mechanism exists.
- The worker polls `wl` commands periodically but does not track work-item state changes post-dispatch.

## Desired change

1. **Extend the dispatch log schema** to support pane-close and state-change entries with outcome reasons.
2. **Add a pane-lifecycle monitor** that tracks dispatched items after they are spawned, detecting when they reach terminal stages (`intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`) or when audits complete.
3. **Implement auto-close logic** that closes panes based on the detected outcome, with the `implement` exception.
4. **Log all lifecycle events** to the dispatch log with structured entries.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Core dispatch worker; add pane-lifecycle tracking and auto-close logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Extend log entry schema for pane-close outcomes.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — Already tracks pane IDs; may need extension for lifecycle callbacks.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — New tests for pane-close logic.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** — *Log herdr downtime dispatches (item comment + rolling .worklog log)* — existing dispatch logging infrastructure.
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9** — *Work-item ↔ agent-pane association tracker* — `AgentTracker` that maps work items to pane IDs.
- **WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3** — *Remove client-side pane count cap* — panes now deliberately stay open until manually closed (context for why auto-close is new).
- **WL-0MTJQOZ0K007KD40** — *Dispatch-logs skill: generates 24h global dispatch report* — related observability.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should happen to panes for items that reach `in_review` but then revert to a different stage?" — Answer: Log the initial `in_review` arrival; if the pane is still open and the item changes again, log the new state. Only close panes at the specific terminal points defined in AC2–AC5. Source: intake draft.
- Q: "Does 'requires attention' apply to panes that are still actively running (agent in `working` state)?" — Answer: No — "requires attention" applies to panes where the agent session has ended (`done` state) but the work item has not reached a terminal stage (`intake_complete`, `plan_complete`, `in_review`). Source: intake draft.
- Q: "Should the worker proactively close panes, or just log and signal?" — Answer: The worker should both log AND close the pane (except for implement). The pane close is an active action. Source: intake draft.

# Pre-dialog gate in worklist.ts + Code Freeze on confirm

## Summary
Integrate the ship guard into the worklist's Ship It flow: pre-dialog gate that blocks opening the confirmation dialog when live panes exist, and write the code-freeze marker on confirm before dispatching the release command, with best-effort cleanup on failure.

## Parent AC Coverage
This task covers parent ACs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5:
- Parent AC 0: "Pressing the Ship It shortcut (`S`) ... does **not** open the Ship It confirmation dialog." — guard runs before `openShipItDialog()`; modal notice shown instead.
- Parent AC 1: "The blocking check runs **before** the confirmation dialog is rendered." — guard runs in the chord-resolution branch before any dialog logic.
- Parent AC 2: "A pane only blocks when it hosts a **live** agent." — guard's `listBlockingPanes` filters by live agent status.
- Parent AC 3: "When no blocking pane exists, pressing `S` opens the Ship It confirmation dialog exactly as today." — if guard returns empty, flow continues to `openShipItDialog()`.
- Parent AC 4: "On typing `ship` + Enter, the worklist writes the Code Freeze marker ... **before** dispatching `/skill:ship release`." — `onConfirm` writes marker before `executeResolvedCommand`.
- Parent AC 5: "If dispatching `/skill:ship release` fails, the worklist best-effort removes the Code Freeze marker." — try/catch around dispatch clears marker on failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] When the resolved command is `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`, the guard runs before `openShipItDialog()`. If blocking panes exist, a modal notice is displayed (listing the panes/work-item IDs) and the dialog is NOT opened.
- [ ] The blocked notice uses the existing in-pane modal notice pattern (like `code-freezeNotice`), dismissible via Esc/Enter/q.
- [ ] In `openShipItDialog`'s `onConfirm` (after user types `ship` + Enter), the code-freeze marker is written **before** calling `executeResolvedCommand(SHIP_IT_COMMAND, ...)`.
- [ ] If dispatching `/skill:ship release` fails (onCommand throws or is a no-op), the marker is best-effort cleared and the error is surfaced to the operator.
- [ ] No regression: when no blocking panes exist, the Ship It dialog opens exactly as before.
- [ ] The typed-confirmation behaviour (case-insensitive `ship`, Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel, bottom-anchored overlay) is unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation
- Modify `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:
  - In the `SHIP_IT_COMMAND` chord-resolution branch, run the guard before `openShipItDialog()`.
  - In `openShipItDialog`'s `onConfirm`, add marker write before dispatch and cleanup on failure.
- Dependencies: `ship-guard.ts` (new), `code-freeze.ts` (extended).

## Deliverables
- Modified `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
